chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Rabie, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no person who insults (verbally) in the eye of a believer except that he will die with the worst of deaths, and it is fitting that he does not return to goodness.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of insulting a believer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes the severity of slandering a believer, linking it to a 'bad death' (*sharr al-mawt*) and spiritual stagnation. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that verbal abuse (*ghibah* or *sabb*) inflicts a wound on the soul comparable to physical injury, potentially severing the individual's connection to divine mercy and leading to a premature or painful end.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Rabie, from Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is none from a person who insults (verbally) in the eye of a Momin except he would die with the most evil of deaths, and he would depart such that he would not return to goodness’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Rib’i from al-Fudayl from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever reviles a believer face-to-face dies in the worst condition and deserves not to find any goodness.’”
